content.text: {"relation":"NOVEL","consensus_summary":"The pearl symbolizes the Kingdom of Heaven (or salvation/Christ) as a treasure of supreme worth, worth surrendering everything to obtain (Matt 13:45-46), with secondary senses of holy truth not to be profaned (Matt 7:6), the glory of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:21), a reversed reading in which Christ is the merchant purchasing the church/believer, and a negative valence of worldly luxury (1 Tim 2:9; Rev 17-18). Wisdom's price 'above pearls/rubies' appears only as a minor thematic note in two responses.","book_summary":"The pearl is 'the one complete light': via the Hebrew peninim, wisdom and the bride are priced above pearls, and the singular pearl of the night sky is the full moon (keseh, 'fulness,' linked to 'throne' and 'time appointed'), governor of the appointed times; the one-pearl gates of the city are the merchant's entry at the King's gate. The book relegates the kingdom/church readings to a 'commonly taught' note distinct from its own identification.","consensus_core_identification":"Pearl = the Kingdom of Heaven / salvation (or Christ, or the redeemed) as the thing of supreme spiritual value.","book_core_identification":"Pearl = the full moon as the one complete light governing the appointed times, tied to wisdom/the bride whose price is above pearls, and to the one-pearl gates as the appointed entry.","core_relation":"COMPATIBLE_OVERLAP","extension_relation":"DIFFERENT_REFERENT","boundary_disagreement":"The book pulls the symbol away from the parable's value-economics (kingdom worth everything) and re-centers it on a calendrical-celestial referent: the full moon and appointed feast times (Ps 81:3; Ps 104:19), plus wisdom/the bride via the peninim wordplay (Prov 3:15; 31:10). It retains Rev 21:21's one-pearl gates but reinterprets them as the appointed lunar entry rather than heavenly glory generally. No consensus response includes any lunar or appointed-times referent; only a marginal wisdom overlap exists (Job 28 notes in Responses C and D).","material_contradiction":"No explicit denial of the consensus is stated; the book prints the kingdom/church reading as the 'commonly taught' view alongside its own, offering a new referent rather than asserting the common one is false. The full-moon identification is absent from, rather than logically incompatible with, the consensus senses.","rationale":"The book's central identification — the pearl as the full moon (keseh, 'fulness'), governor of appointed times, with wisdom/the bride priced above pearls — appears in none of the four consensus responses, neither as primary meaning nor as any listed alternative. The nearest contact point is the minor wisdom-above-pearls motif (Job 28 / Prov 3:15) mentioned peripherally in Responses C and D, but that is not the book's core, which is the lunar-calendrical reading. Because the book does not directly contradict the kingdom-of-heaven identification (it acknowledges it as the common view) but introduces a referent no consensus stream covers, the correct classification is NOVEL rather than DIVERGENT or REFINED.","citation_support":"INSUFFICIENT","strongest_objection":"One could argue DIVERGENT: the book effectively replaces the parable's and Rev 21:21's consensus referent (kingdom/heavenly glory) with the moon and appointed times, and treating the common view as merely 'commonly taught' signals replacement. Alternatively, one could argue the wisdom-priced-above-pearls element is already a listed minority alternative, nudging toward REFINED. But the decisive core — pearl as full moon — is neither a boundary adjustment of the kingdom reading nor its logical negation, so NOVEL best fits.","confidence":"medium"}
